key_insight: GITIII is a lightweight, interpretable graph transformer that learns correlations between cell state and niche in a self-supervised way to infer spatial single-cell interactions and quantify how neighbouring cells influence a receiver cell's gene expression.
problem_solved: Inferring cell–cell interactions and quantifying neighbour influence from spatial transcriptomics data is challenging due to high dimensionality, local context dependence and the need for interpretable, scalable models.
method: Self-supervised graph transformer that encodes cells as nodes and spatial/neighbour relations as graph structure to learn joint cell-state and niche representations.
Interpretable attention/attribution mechanism to quantify per-neighbour influence on a receiver cell's gene expression and to highlight interaction patterns.
Lightweight architecture optimized for single-cell spatial resolution to allow scalable inference across tissues while preserving interpretability.
impact: Provides ML practitioners a scalable, interpretable framework to derive biologically meaningful cell–cell interaction maps from spatial transcriptomics, enabling better downstream analysis, hypothesis generation, and integration of transformer/GNN techniques in spatial biology.
visual_elements: Schematic of the graph transformer: cells as nodes, spatial edges, and attention layers showing learned weights
Tissue map overlay: cells colored by inferred influence score from specific neighbours (heatmap on tissue image)
Cell–cell interaction network: weighted edges (thickness/color) indicating strength/direction of influence
Flowchart of self-supervised training → representation learning → attribution/interpretation
paper_title: Inferring spatial single-cell-level interactions through interpreting cell state and niche correlations learned by self-supervised graph transformer
paper_authors: Xiao Xiao, Le Zhang, Hongyu Zhao, Zuoheng Wang
